title: Batch or real-time? Ask who is waiting and whether tools loop
head: Workload
Right interface
Why
rows: Batch has no tool loop per request
rule: Batch saves 50% but promises nothing about time. Use it for work nobody is blocked on.

title: Batch request stops at tool_use: what can you do?
head: Situation
Right move
Why
rows: Tool data predictable and available beforehand
Pre-fetch it into each batch request
Model must decide what to look up as it goes
Synchronous requests with a tool loop
Batch has no multi-turn tool calling
No need to redo the batch
Model answers in text instead of calling a tool
rule: Batch requests can't run tool loops. If the tool data is predictable, fetch it first and keep the discount.

title: Batch results: what links each result back to its input?
head: Situation
Right mechanism
Why
rows: Each item needs several tool calls
rule: Batch results come back in any order. Give each request a custom_id, match on it, and resubmit only failed IDs.

title: Batch or real-time? Ask who waits, and for how long
head: Situation
Right choice
Why
rows: Non-blocking, read the next day (overnight report, weekly audit)
Non-blocking but a person must act within a deadline
Needs multi-turn tool calling in one request
Some requests in a batch failed
rule: Batch only work that nobody waits on by a deadline. Non-blocking is not the same as latency-tolerant.

title: Cutting cost: which levers keep the output complete?
head: Lever
When it fits
Watch out for
rows: No latency SLA; no multi-turn tools
Trim input to the fields the task uses
Requests carry content the task ignores
rule: Batch what nobody waits for; trim what the task doesn't read. Don't skip work a requirement says to cover.

title: Big extraction job: batch or real-time?
head: Situation
Right approach
Why
rows: Each document needs multi-turn tool calls
Keep it separate from the backfill
rule: Not urgent, single-call, large volume → Message Batches API with custom_id.
